narration_text: Cities are getting hotter, and it is not just climate change. It is something built into the concrete itself.
Urban centers can run up to seven degrees Celsius hotter than the countryside around them.
Three things drive it. Dark asphalt absorbs heat. Buildings block cooling wind. And cars plus AC units pump out waste heat all day.
And it is accelerating. The number of extreme heat days in major cities has more than doubled since the nineteen eighties.
As one climate scientist put it, we did not just build cities in a warming world. We built machines that make the warming worse.

key_data.quote: We built machines that make the warming worse.

narration_text: The fix is surprisingly simple. Painting a roof white can cut its surface temperature by up to thirty degrees compared to a black roof.
Trees, white roofs, and smarter streets. The heat is a design problem. And design problems have design solutions.
